intro.text: A land of Roshar, off whose northern coast live the greatshells called yu-nerig.
A nation on the isthmus between the Purelake and the Reshi Sea, bordered by Tu Bayla to the east and Babatharnam to the west.

description.text: The yu-nerig are prized for their succulent meat and their gemhearts.
Marabethians love to argue. Pedestals stand at street intersections so that men can climb up and declaim, and listeners are said to carry overripe fruit to discourage speakers they disagree with.

Serious criminals are hung over a seaside cliff at high tide, cheeks cut, as bait for the yu-nerig, and freed if they survive a week; most are attacked within a day. They may demand execution instead, but nearly all prefer false hope to certain death.
Marabethians believe sarpenthyn are the vengeful spirits of murdered children.
Marabethia has several local monarchs and is more a group of culturally similar states than a single nation. A city may be led by a high minister, and high judges are important keepers of the law.

High judges wear a patterned shoulder cloak and a colourful skirt-like wrap. Men wear a garment called the Marabethian wrap, and a woman may wear just a cloth tied around her chest in place of a shirt.
Part of the population follows the Purelaker religion, especially in the south near the Purelake.

The Skybreakers keep a stronghold on the southern edge along the Purelake, where they train acolytes. The government calls on them for help with enforcement and has granted them legal authority in the region.

Singers lived in the land before humans came to Roshar. Some time after settling in what is now Shinovar, humans invaded, killing or driving out the singers and taking the land. This history was forgotten until the Eila Stele was found.
The land was ruled by the Silver Kingdom of Sela Tales, with its far eastern edge in Valhav, and it is still counted among the Selay lands.
After Aharietiam, Sela Tales broke apart into many smaller states, some of which became Marabethia.
Lift spent time in Marabethia, where the man she called Darkness pursued her, before she moved on to Azir.
The coalition of monarchs asked Marabethia for aid and alliance, but it did not respond.

In 1174, Szeth and his fellow acolytes were brought to a town on the southern border, which held prisoners from across the region, to hunt down inmates who had escaped its jail. The jail keeper was caught and found guilty of pocketing funds meant for the prison.

told.title: Taken from the singers
told.text: Singers lived here before humans came to Roshar. Some time after settling in what is now Shinovar, humans invaded, killing or driving out the singers and claiming the land. The story was forgotten until the Eila Stele was found.

told.title: Part of Sela Tales
told.text: In the age of the Silver Kingdoms this land belonged to Sela Tales. It is still counted among the Selay lands.

told.title: Desolation after Desolation
told.text: Desolations struck this land again and again, along with the rest of Roshar.

told.title: Desolation after Desolation
told.text: Desolations struck this land again and again, along with the rest of Roshar, each one throwing people back to stone tools until the returning Heralds helped them rebuild, often as far as bronze.

told.title: The Desolations end
told.text: After the Last Desolation, no more Desolations came to ravage the nations, and society grew stronger than ever before.

told.title: A cluster of states
told.text: By the present day Sela Tales was long gone, and in its place Marabethia was less a true nation than a cluster of states sharing one culture, with several local monarchs.

told.title: Lift passes through
told.text: Lift spent time in Marabethia, hunted by a man she called Darkness, before moving on to Azir.

told.title: No answer to the coalition
told.text: When the True Desolation came, the coalition of monarchs asked Marabethia for aid and alliance. It never replied.

told.title: Skybreakers hunt escaped prisoners
told.text: Szeth and his fellow acolytes were sent to a town on the southern border, home to Reshi idealists and to a jail for prisoners from across the region, to track down inmates who had broken out. The jail keeper was caught and convicted of pocketing money meant for the prison's upkeep.
